agency: U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Human Services (DHS), Division of Family Assistance (DFA)
agency_short: U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Human Services (DHS)
admin_note: The U.S. Virgin Islands is a TERRITORY that runs standard federal SNAP directly — NOT the Nutrition Assistance Program (NAP) block grant that Puerto Rico, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands run instead. This pack independently re-confirmed that distinction from two primary USDA sources before building anything: USDA's own SNAP directory entry for the Virgin Islands (fns.usda.gov/snap-directory-entry/virgin-islands, page title 'Virgin Islands Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)') and USDA's 17th-edition State Options Report (December 2025, data as of 10/1/2024), whose own introduction states plainly: 'SNAP State agencies include all 50 States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and the Virgin Islands.' DHS administers SNAP centrally through its Division of Family Assistance (DFA) across three district offices — St. Croix (STX), St. Thomas (STT), and St. John (STJ) — with no separate county-level policy authority, structurally similar to this roster's other state-administered packs (Delaware, Nebraska, Connecticut, etc.). GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING distinctive to this pack: unlike every prior state pack in this roster, this pack found NO online self-service SNAP application portal for the Virgin Islands (no equivalent of Delaware ASSIST, BenefitsCal, or a state-run web portal) — applicants must print or pick up a paper 'SNAP/Cash Assistance Combined Application,' then submit it in person, by mail, by email, by fax, or via a district-office drop box. This pack treats the absence of a digital portal as a genuine, disclosed access-model difference, not a research gap — DHS-VI's own Family Assistance Programs page lists these submission channels explicitly and describes no online submission option.
system: DHS's Division of Family Assistance (DFA) administers SNAP centrally for the territory, with three district offices (St. Croix, St. Thomas, St. John), each with its own phone extension. USVI's EBT card carries a distinctive local nickname: DHS's own SNAP consumer content calls it the 'sun, sand & sea' card. USVI is one of only four SNAP jurisdictions (with Alaska, Hawaii, and Guam) that receives a COLA-adjusted income/deduction table structurally different from the 48 contiguous states plus DC, per USDA's own program-design note. USVI has adopted Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) at a 175% federal-poverty-guideline gross-income gate with NO resource/asset limit for any household — confirmed directly on USDA's own current BBCE policy page (fna.usda.gov/snap/broad-based-categorical-eligibility), not merely a secondary-source claim. USVI fully opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP disqualification ('No disqualification'), confirmed via USDA's own 17th-edition State Options Report. All USVI SNAP households are on simplified reporting only, with certification periods of 6, 12, or 24 months depending on household circumstance (per the same USDA report); this pack could not locate a USVI-specific breakdown of which households receive which certification length and discloses this as a gap. USVI does NOT appear on USDA's current published list of states operating a Restaurant Meals Program.

verification.method: This pack's first and most consequential step was independently re-verifying the SNAP-vs-NAP distinction this codebase's packs.ts comment already asserts for the Virgin Islands, rather than trusting the existing comment at face value — confirmed via two separate primary USDA sources (the FNS/FNA SNAP state directory entry and the 17th-edition State Options Report's own introductory text). All USDA fns.usda.gov and dhs.vi.gov/vi.gov fetches returned clean HTTP 200 to a standard browser User-Agent with no WAF/bot-detection barrier of the kind several mainland-state packs in this roster encountered — a genuinely easier access profile than, e.g., New Hampshire or Maine. One naming/branding wrinkle noted: USDA's own site now displays 'Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA)' rather than 'Food and Nutrition Service (FNS)' as of a June 1, 2026 rename the site itself discloses via a banner ('As of June 1, 2026 the Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) is now the Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA)'); this pack cites the historical fns.usda.gov URLs since those are what currently resolve and were fetched, and notes the rename for future packs' awareness. The one substantive fetch judgment call: DHS-VI's own FY2026 COLA table contains an internally ambiguous income-column layout with BOTH a '175% of Poverty' and a '200% of Poverty' gross-income column side by side, whereas USDA's own official BBCE policy page states plainly and singularly that the Virgin Islands' BBCE gross-income gate is 175% FPL with no asset limit — this pack treats USDA's own official BBCE page as authoritative for the applicable categorical-eligibility gate and flags the DHS-VI table's second, unexplained 200% column as an unresolved internal ambiguity rather than guessing at its purpose.
verification.gates: No WAF or bot-detection barrier was encountered against fns.usda.gov, dhs.vi.gov, or vi.gov with a standard browser User-Agent; all served clean HTTP 200 responses to direct curl and WebFetch attempts, a notably easier profile than several mainland packs in this roster. All PDFs (the FY2026 COLA table, simplified-reporting requirements, ABAWD webpage and flyer PDFs, and the 114-page USDA 17th-edition State Options Report) fetched cleanly and converted cleanly with pdftotext -layout. No Wayback Machine fallback or reader-proxy workaround was needed for any USVI-specific source in this pack, unlike Delaware's usda.gov 403 or New Hampshire/Maine's WAF walls.
